summary: This article explains why the Amazon Rainforest is the world's largest rainforest, the huge variety of life it holds, and why people call it the "lungs of the Earth."
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “The Amazon Rainforest” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: the thick roof of leaves formed by the tallest trees in a forest
a particular kind of plant or animal
the process plants use to turn sunlight into food and release oxygen

challengeTerms.def: all the living things in an area together with their environment
describing matter that is breaking down after a plant or animal dies
originally living in a place, rather than arriving from somewhere else

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that protecting faraway forests like the Amazon is not something ordinary people can really affect? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why the Amazon Rainforest matters to the whole planet, not just to the countries where it is located.
struggling: Pre-teach canopy, species, and photosynthesis with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses ecosystem, decomposing, and indigenous to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
